This is the **Deno** runtime source repository. Here's the overview:

## Total size: ~11,800 files across 6 main directories

---

### `cli/` — 493 files
The user-facing CLI binary (`deno`). Key sub-areas:
- `args/` — flag and subcommand parsing (`flags.rs`)
- `tools/` — one file/folder per subcommand: `fmt`, `lint`, `test`, `check`, `compile`, `repl`, `run`, `serve`, `task`, `doc`, `coverage`, `publish`, `upgrade`, `jupyter`, etc.
- `lsp/` — language server protocol implementation (used by editor extensions)
- `tsc/` — TypeScript compiler integration
- `standalone/` — `deno compile` self-contained binary logic
- `snapshot/` — V8 snapshot creation for fast startup
- `lib/` — shared CLI library crate (`deno_lib`)

### `ext/` — 621 files
Native extensions that expose system APIs to JavaScript. Each is its own Rust crate:
- Web APIs: `web`, `webidl`, `fetch`, `websocket`, `webstorage`, `url`, `broadcast_channel`
- I/O & networking: `fs`, `net`, `io`, `http`, `tls`
- System: `os`, `process`, `signals`, `ffi` (foreign function interface)
- Crypto: `crypto`, `node_crypto`
- Storage: `kv` (Deno KV), `cache`, `node_sqlite`
- Other: `napi` (Node.js native addon API), `webgpu`, `image`, `cron`, `telemetry`, `bundle`

### `libs/` — 729 files
Internal shared library crates, not tied to a single extension:
- `core` / `dcore` — the V8 JS engine integration (`deno_core`)
- `serde_v8` — serialization between Rust and V8 values
- `npm`, `npm_cache`, `npm_installer`, `npmrc` — npm compatibility
- `node_resolver`, `node_shim` — Node.js module resolution
- `resolver`, `config`, `lockfile` — Deno module resolution and config
- `eszip` — bundled module archive format
- `ops` — proc-macro for defining Rust ops exposed to JS
- `inspector_server` — Chrome DevTools protocol inspector
- Others: `crypto`, `dotenv`, `cache_dir`, `package_json`, `typescript_go_client`

### `runtime/` — 72 files
Assembles all extensions into the `deno_runtime` crate:
- `permissions/` — the permission system (allow/deny flags)
- `features/` — runtime feature flags
- `ops/` — runtime-level ops (workers, signals, etc.)
- `js/` — JavaScript bootstrap code for the runtime
- `subprocess_windows/` — Windows-specific subprocess handling

### `tests/` — 9,725 files (bulk of the repo)
- `specs/` — primary integration tests: each folder has a `__test__.jsonc` + expected output
- `unit/` — Deno-side unit tests (TypeScript)
- `unit_node/` — Node.js compatibility unit tests
- `testdata/` — fixture files for tests
- `node_compat/` — Node.js compat test suite
- `wpt/` — Web Platform Tests
- `ffi/`, `napi/` — native addon tests
- `bench/`, `bench_util/` — benchmark infrastructure
- `integration/`, `util/` — integration test helpers

### `tools/` — 52 files
Developer tooling scripts (JS/TS):
- `format.js`, `lint.js` — code quality scripts (referenced in CLAUDE.md)
- `release/` — release automation
- `napi/` — NAPI build helpers
- `lint_plugins/` — custom lint rules

---

**Bottom line:** this is the full Deno monorepo — a Rust/TypeScript runtime with ~60 Cargo crates organized around a CLI, a runtime assembler, per-API native extensions, shared libraries, and a large integration test suite.

baseline.answer:
Now I have the complete picture. Here is the full call chain for `Deno.readFile()` tracing from the public API to the OS syscall.

---

## Call Chain: `Deno.readFile(path)` → OS `read(2)` syscall

### Layer 1 — Public JS API
**`runtime/js/90_deno_ns.js:56`**
```js
// Deno namespace object, assembled at startup
readFile: fs.readFile,
```
`Deno.readFile` is just a re-export from the `ext:deno_fs` module. The `Deno` global itself is built here and frozen on the global scope.

---

### Layer 2 — JS Implementation (ext/fs)
**`ext/fs/30_fs.js:773`**
```js
async function readFile(path, options) {
  // ...abort signal / cancel handle setup...
  const read = await op_fs_read_file_async(pathFromURL(path), cancelRid);
  return read;
}
```
Resolves the path (handling `URL` objects), sets up an optional `AbortSignal` cancel handle, then crosses the JS→Rust boundary by calling the registered op `op_fs_read_file_async`.

---

### Layer 3 — Op Dispatch (deno_core bridge)
**`ext/fs/ops.rs:1513`** — `#[op2(stack_trace)] pub async fn op_fs_read_file_async`

The `#[op2]` proc-macro registers this Rust function as a callable op name. This is the V8 → Rust boundary. Responsibilities here:
1. **Permission check** — calls `PermissionsContainer::check_open(path, OpenAccessKind::Read, "Deno.readFile()")` which enforces `--allow-read`.
2. **Cancellation** — looks up an optional `CancelHandle` resource from the resource table.
3. **Dispatch** — calls `fs.read_file_async(path, options)` on the injected `FileSystemRc`.

---

### Layer 4 — FileSystem trait (interface.rs)
**`ext/fs/interface.rs:376`** — `FileSystem::read_file_async` default impl
```rust
async fn read_file_async(&self, path, options) -> FsResult<Cow<[u8]>> {
    let file = self.open_async(path, options).await?;
    let buf  = file.read_all_async().await?;
    Ok(buf)
}
```
This is a default method on the `FileSystem` trait. It calls `open_async` then `read_all_async` — both also trait methods, allowing different implementations (real FS, in-memory FS for testing, etc.) to be swapped in.

The concrete type in production is **`RealFs`** (`cli/factory.rs:512`):
```rust
self.services.fs.get_or_init(|| Arc::new(RealFs))
```

---

### Layer 5 — RealFs implementation (std_fs.rs)
**`ext/fs/std_fs.rs:457`** — `RealFs::read_file_async`
```rust
async fn read_file_async(&self, path, options) -> FsResult<Cow<[u8]>> {
    let mut file = open_with_checked_path(options, &path)?;
    spawn_blocking(move || {
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        file.read_to_end(&mut buf)?;  // <-- std::io::Read
        Ok(Cow::Owned(buf))
    }).await?
}
```
Two things happen here:
- `open_with_checked_path` → `open_options_for_checked_path` → `std::fs::OpenOptions::open(path)` — this is the `open(2)` syscall.
- The blocking read is offloaded to **Tokio's `spawn_blocking` thread pool** (`deno_core::unsync::spawn_blocking`) to avoid blocking the async executor, and `file.read_to_end()` calls `std::io::Read` which maps to the `read(2)` syscall.

---

### Layer 6 — OS / stdlib
**`std::fs::File::read_to_end`** → `std::io::Read` impl → **`libc::read(fd, buf, count)`** / `ReadFile` on Windows.

---

## Summary table

| Layer | Location | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Public API | `runtime/js/90_deno_ns.js:56` | Re-exports `fs.readFile` onto `Deno` global |
| 2. JS impl | `ext/fs/30_fs.js:773` | URL resolution, abort signal, calls op |
| 3. Op dispatch | `ext/fs/ops.rs:1513` | V8→Rust bridge; enforces `--allow-read` permissions |
| 4. `FileSystem` trait | `ext/fs/interface.rs:376` | Abstraction layer; `open_async` + `read_all_async` |
| 5. `RealFs` impl | `ext/fs/std_fs.rs:457` | Opens file via `std::fs`; reads on Tokio blocking thread |
| 6. OS | `std::io::Read` / libc | `open(2)` + `read(2)` syscalls |

The key design points are:
- The **`FileSystem` trait** at layer 4 is the seam that allows swapping real I/O for a virtual FS (e.g., in `deno compile` standalone mode — see `cli/rt/file_system.rs`).
- The **permission check** in layer 3 is the single enforcement point for `--allow-read`, making it impossible to bypass via the JS API.
- **Async file reads use `spawn_blocking`** because POSIX file I/O is not natively async — Tokio moves the blocking `read(2)` call off the event-loop thread.

|---|---|---|

## Subprocesses Spawned at Runtime

| Subprocess | Triggering code | When |
|---|---|---|
| **`tar.exe` / `unzip`** | `cli/util/archive.rs:19,37` | `deno upgrade` on Windows/Unix — extracts downloaded archive |
| **`gh` (GitHub CLI)** | `cli/tools/upgrade.rs:611,622,674,726,829,845,896` | `deno upgrade --canary` via GitHub Actions / PR builds |
| **`powershell.exe`** | `cli/tools/upgrade.rs:1602` | Windows: updating `PATH` after upgrade |
| **`node` / `npm` / `npx`** | `cli/task_runner.rs:270,311,402` | `deno task` running npm lifecycle scripts |
| **`git`** | `cli/tools/publish/mod.rs:1253,1266` | `deno publish` — reading git metadata for provenance |
| **`cat` / `cmd.exe`** | `cli/lsp/parent_process_checker.rs:65` | LSP mode — detecting if parent process (editor) is still alive |
| **`sysctl` / `wmic`** | `cli/tools/bench/mitata.rs:109,125` | `deno bench` — reading CPU info for benchmark output |
| **`deno` (self)** | `cli/lib.rs:1049`, `cli/tools/x.rs:93` | `deno compile` subprocess, `deno x` shim |
| **Arbitrary user binary** | `ext/process/lib.rs` via `Deno.Command` / `deno_task_shell` | User code calling `new Deno.Command(…)` or shell tasks |

---

### Key takeaways

- **All import-time network calls** go through `cli/file_fetcher.rs` → `reqwest`/`hyper`, gated by the permission system (`runtime/permissions`).
- **JSR and npm registries** are the two mandatory external registries; both are URL-overridable via env vars (`$JSR_URL`, `$NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`).
- **OpenTelemetry** has no hardcoded endpoint — it only fires when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set.
- **Panic reporting** and the **background update checker** are the only "phone home" calls made without explicit user action; the update checker is throttled and can be suppressed.
- **Sigstore/Fulcio/Rekor** are only contacted during `deno publish` with provenance signing.

## Call Chain: `vm.$mount()` → DOM I/O

This is the Vue 2.x source tree. The primary I/O is **DOM mutation** (no network or file I/O in the core rendering path). There is also a secondary async scheduling I/O layer via `Promise.then` / `MutationObserver` / `setTimeout`.

---

### Layer 1 — Public API: `vm.$mount(el)`
**`src/platforms/web/runtime/index.ts:36`**

The top-level entry point. Resolves the `el` string/element via `query(el)`, then immediately delegates:
```ts
return mountComponent(this, el, hydrating)
```

---

### Layer 2 — Component Lifecycle Orchestration: `mountComponent()`
**`src/core/instance/lifecycle.ts:147`**

Defines the `updateComponent` closure and hands it to a `Watcher`:
```ts
updateComponent = () => { vm._update(vm._render(), hydrating) }
new Watcher(vm, updateComponent, noop, watcherOptions, true)
```
The `Watcher` constructor immediately evaluates `updateComponent` for the initial render. On subsequent reactive changes it re-queues via `queueWatcher`.

---

### Layer 3 — Reactivity / Scheduling: `Watcher` + `queueWatcher` + `nextTick`
**`src/core/observer/watcher.ts`**, **`src/core/observer/scheduler.ts`**, **`src/core/util/next-tick.ts`**

When observed data changes, the chain is:
```
Dep.notify() → watcher.update() → queueWatcher(this)
  → nextTick(flushSchedulerQueue)         [scheduler.ts:~170]
    → timerFunc()                         [next-tick.ts:42]
      → Promise.resolve().then(flushCallbacks)   ← primary (microtask I/O)
      or MutationObserver / setImmediate / setTimeout  ← fallbacks
    → flushSchedulerQueue() → watcher.run() → updateComponent()
```
This is where **async scheduling I/O** happens — `nextTick` defers DOM writes to the microtask queue (or a macrotask if `Promise` is unavailable).

---

### Layer 4 — Virtual DOM Rendering: `vm._render()`
**`src/core/instance/render.ts:103`**

Produces a **virtual DOM tree** (no real DOM touched yet):
```ts
vnode = render.call(vm._renderProxy, vm.$createElement)
```
The compiled render function calls `vm.$createElement` (or `vm._c`), which flows into `src/core/vdom/create-element.ts` and returns a tree of `VNode` objects.

---

### Layer 5 — VNode Reconciliation: `vm._update()` → `__patch__()`
**`src/core/instance/lifecycle.ts:63`** → **`src/platforms/web/runtime/patch.ts:10`**

`_update` calls the platform-injected patch function:
```ts
vm.$el = vm.__patch__(prevVnode, vnode)
```
`__patch__` is created by `createPatchFunction({ nodeOps, modules })` — the factory closes over `nodeOps` so the core diff algorithm is platform-agnostic.

---

### Layer 6 — Diff Algorithm: `patch()` / `createElm()` / `patchVnode()`
**`src/core/vdom/patch.ts:66`** (Snabbdom-based)

Walks the old and new VNode trees. For new nodes, calls `createElm()`:
- `src/core/vdom/patch.ts:121` — `createElm(vnode, insertedVnodeQueue, parentElm, refElm)`
  - Dispatches to `nodeOps.createElement(tag, vnode)` for element nodes
  - `nodeOps.createTextNode(text)` for text nodes
  - `nodeOps.createComment(text)` for comment nodes
  - Then calls `insert(parentElm, vnode.elm, refElm)` → `nodeOps.insertBefore` or `nodeOps.appendChild`

For existing nodes, `patchVnode()` diffs props/attrs/children and calls module hooks (class, style, attrs, events, dom-props).

---

### Layer 7 — Low-Level DOM I/O: `nodeOps.*`
**`src/platforms/web/runtime/node-ops.ts`**

Every function here is a **direct DOM call** — this is the bottom of the stack:

| `nodeOps` function | DOM call |
|---|---|
| `createElement(tag, vnode)` | `document.createElement(tag)` |
| `createElementNS(ns, tag)` | `document.createElementNS(...)` |
| `createTextNode(text)` | `document.createTextNode(text)` |
| `createComment(text)` | `document.createComment(text)` |
| `appendChild(node, child)` | `node.appendChild(child)` |
| `insertBefore(parent, node, ref)` | `parent.insertBefore(node, ref)` |
| `removeChild(node, child)` | `node.removeChild(child)` |
| `setTextContent(node, text)` | `node.textContent = text` |
| `setStyleScope(node, id)` | `node.setAttribute(id, '')` |

---

### Summary diagram

```
vm.$mount(el)                          [web/runtime/index.ts:36]
  └─ mountComponent(vm, el)            [core/instance/lifecycle.ts:147]
       └─ new Watcher(vm, updateComponent)   [core/observer/watcher.ts]
            │  (on data change: queueWatcher → nextTick)
            │       └─ Promise.then / MutationObserver / setTimeout  ◄── ASYNC I/O
            └─ updateComponent()
                 ├─ vm._render()             [core/instance/render.ts:103]
                 │    └─ render(vm.$createElement)  → VNode tree (pure JS)
                 └─ vm._update(vnode)        [core/instance/lifecycle.ts:63]
                      └─ vm.__patch__(old, new)   [core/vdom/patch.ts via createPatchFunction]
                           └─ createElm / patchVnode
                                └─ nodeOps.*      [web/runtime/node-ops.ts]
                                     └─ document.createElement / appendChild / ...  ◄── DOM I/O
```

**Intermediate layers in order:** public mount API → lifecycle orchestration → reactivity/scheduling (async I/O) → virtual DOM rendering → VNode diff algorithm → platform node-ops abstraction → raw DOM API calls.
